title: a command withheld for having nothing to run was accounted for nowhere
body:
# 0013: a command withheld for having nothing to run was accounted for nowhere

## Tags

help, activation, D11, accounting, no-silent-errors, recurrence-of-0001

## Summary

A built-in command whose language column is `any`, but all of whose OPTIONS are language-scoped and inactive, was withheld correctly and explained nowhere. It appeared in neither `help`'s listing nor `help --why`'s "Not offered here" block, and the dispatcher reported it as **unknown**.

Reported by hv, on a Riffle install whose `languages:` was still commented out:

    ❯ pwd && bin/riffle test all
    /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Riffle
    Riffle: unknown command: test (try: bin/Riffle help)

    "Also, why doesn't 'test all' work?"

`test` is not an unknown command. devbin ships it, and it could not run anything.

## The withholding itself is CORRECT and is not what changed

`command_active` withholds a command with options once none of them survives, and `lib/resolve` already says why: *"A `test` that exists but can run nothing would offer an empty `all` and report success for having run zero gates -- the false green the sealed gates exist to prevent."*

That is right and is untouched. The defect is entirely in the accounting.

## Mechanism

`command_unavailable_reason` is the single function both callers use to explain a withheld command -- `lib/help` for `--why`, `bin/devbin` for the dispatcher's refusal. Its language branch read:

    project_speaks "$lang" && return 1
    printf "this project does not declare the '%s' language\n" "$lang"

`test`'s catalogue row is `any`, and `project_speaks` returns true for `any`. So the function returned 1 -- **no reason available** -- for a command that was demonstrably not available. From there:

- `_print_unavailable` (help) does `command_active "$cmd" || continue`, a bare `continue` with no row printed, so the command vanished from both lists.
- `bin/devbin` fell through to `unknown command`.

Two symptoms, one missing branch.

`help --why` advertises itself in its own output as *"The listing, plus what is not here and why."* A command that is not here and gets no why is that promise broken, and it is the same family as issues 0001 and 0009: devbin offering, or failing to account for, something on an activation axis that does not match the consumer.

## The asymmetry that makes it visible

`build` and `test` have identical catalogue rows -- both `any`, both a `-` command line. In a project declaring no languages, `build` is OFFERED with an explanatory origin line ("devbin ships the name only -- declare commands.build.run or add bin/.devbin/cmd/build"), and `test` disappears completely. The difference is that `build` ships no options at all while `test` ships options that are all inactive, and only one of those two states had an explanation attached.

## Resolution

One branch in `command_unavailable_reason`, which fixes both callers at once -- the reason it belongs there and not in the help renderer:

    if project_speaks "$lang"; then
      if [ -n "$(builtin_options "$cmd")" ] || [ -n "$(cfg_list "commands.$cmd.options")" ]; then
        printf 'every option it offers is inactive here, so it would run nothing (declare project.languages in %s, or commands.%s.run)\n' ...
        return 0
      fi
      return 1
    fi

Two tests in `tests/unit/help.bats`, both red-checked first, one per caller. The dispatcher's red-check reproduces hv's report verbatim: `demo: unknown command: test (try: bin/demo help)`.

## Notes

The fix makes the message tell you what to do, which is the whole point:

    $ bin/riffle test all           # before
    Riffle: unknown command: test (try: bin/Riffle help)

    $ bin/demo test all             # after
    every option it offers is inactive here, so it would run nothing
    (declare project.languages in bin/.devbin/config.yaml, or commands.test.run)

At Riffle the answer was `languages: [elixir]`, left commented out by `install`'s starter config. With it declared, `test mix` seals green at 282 passed.
